criterionFindings.criterion: A goal entered WITHOUT technical detail produces a reviewable draft in demo mode
criterionFindings.basis: Re-ran tests/e2e/intent/journey.test.ts myself in a real browser after a sanctioned runtime restart: goal-only form -> demo mode -> draft review screen with facts/assumptions/unknowns, blockage count and provenance, exit 0. Source confirms: intake requires only snapshot+goal (intake-screen.tsx:88), orchestrator assembles a server-owned draft via DemoPlannerProvider with revalidation (orchestrator.ts:89-99), demo provider is credential/network-free and visibly fixture-based (demo.ts).

assertTransition requires requiredDecisionsResolved for ready_for_approval/approved (packages/contracts/workflow/index.ts:30) and InternalIntentSchema blocks ready/approved payload state with unresolved required decisions (packages/contracts/private/index.ts:20); store transition enforces it inside the transaction (intent-store.ts:122). Observed in my e2e re-run: readiness 422 missing_evidence before decision resolution, UI button disabled; contract orchestrator tests cover the same gates.

criterionFindings.criterion: Edit-after-approval invalidates affected downstream evidence/approvals; a new revision after approval invalidates the old approval
criterionFindings.basis: Observed in my e2e re-run: POST /v1/intents/:id/revisions after approval -> 201 version 3 draft with approvalInvalidated:true; repeat approval with old version/hash -> 409 stale_version; head read shows supersededApproval:true and the UI shows the invalidation alert. Real-DB session-live fixture (contracts intent suite) confirms approved payload immutability and stale-old-approval rejection. Old approved revision rows stay immutable (approved_hash binds content_hash, intent-store.ts:49,124); future downstream stores bind by intent hash and are invalidated by construction (no downstream artifacts exist yet, M3.2+).

criterionFindings.criterion: Previews use trusted templates/escaped data or an opaque-origin sandbox; proposed code never executes in the private console origin
criterionFindings.basis: Verified BOTH from source and a real browser: source inspection of apps/private-console (intents-screen.tsx, intake-screen.tsx, main.tsx, private-client.ts) shows only React text interpolation with no dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML/document.write/eval/new Function (grep clean over the app). My re-run of the hostile-goal e2e test in Chromium rendered the script/img-onerror/svg-onload/javascript: goal as escaped text: window canaries undefined, zero img/svg/javascript:-link elements, page URL unchanged, exactly one script element (the console bundle), and the review fetch returns application/json. Escaping path used; opaque-origin sandbox not needed since no code-preview content exists at the intent stage (honest limitation).

criterionFindings.criterion: PM can describe a full-stack or codebase-policy outcome; owner can review ONE composed task without being forced to create separate layer bounties
criterionFindings.basis: My e2e re-run of the composed journey: one goal describing selection journey plus response policy produced exactly one reviewable draft whose acceptance examples span selection_ui, selection_api, response_policy and the end-to-end selection_journey; exactly one review article rendered; UI states nothing is split into separate per-layer bounties. Demo fixture selection_with_policy (demo-fixtures.ts:47) backs this without an exclusive discipline discriminator.

criterionFindings.criterion: Owner approval binds the exact reviewed intent revision/hash with private traceability; server-side authority (no client-supplied authority assertion; no bearer capability from a request body)
criterionFindings.basis: Approval route uses intent.approve (owner-only per packages/contracts/auth/policy.ts:7); body schemas are strictObject {expectedVersion, expectedHash} (intents/types.ts:15); orchestrator.approve passes exact version+hash to the store; store.transition re-locks the head row, re-derives the role from private_accounts/private_sessions inside the transaction (intent-store.ts:33-37) and sets approved_by/approved_hash=content_hash only on exact match (intent-store.ts:124). My re-run of the e2e authorization test: requester approval 403, operator every intent route 403, stranger create 404/read 403, wrong hash 422, contributor cookie 401 on private API, external API route 404; contract tests reject request bodies containing endpoint/model/executor/approval/actorRole fields with 400. Minor note: approvedAt reports the revision row's created_at, not the approval-recorded time (see limitations).

criterionFindings.criterion: Internal task objects are never serialized to a contributor route; publicProductFlow remains not_implemented
criterionFindings.basis: Grep of services/external-api shows no intent routes/wiring; my e2e re-run confirms external API returns 404 for intent/request-intent routes and the private API rejects a contributor session with 401 authentication_denied. The review DTO is a schema-enforced positive allowlist (ReviewProjectionSchema strictObject, intents/types.ts:32-49); tests assert exactly 17 keys and absence of workspace paths/private canaries. publicProductFlow not_implemented is asserted in the session-live DB fixture and both e2e structured logs.

criterionFindings.basis: Read all of them myself. server.ts:11-26 wires intents only when auth exists, with a derived-from-intake fallback and no model configuration (so ollama is safely unconfigured); host/origin allowlist hook preserved. main.tsx is a thin shell mounting IntakeScreen/IntentsScreen with CSRF handling. intent-store.ts adds request-bound create with transaction-bound ownership+snapshot-hash binding, ownership-filtered readForRequest by provenance containment, approval traceability and supersededApproval; the legacy string-actor branch is unchanged. trusted.Dockerfile lines 22-23 COPY packages/planner/prompts and providers; dockerignore lines 46-49 allowlist exactly !packages/planner/prompts/** and !packages/planner/providers/** as the handoff requested; the canonical image build (coordinator-runtime-build.json exit 0) and my successful runtime restart plus passing e2e prove the wiring works.

approvedAt in the private approval traceability is the revision row's created_at (revision creation time) rather than the moment approval was recorded; the approval binding itself (approver, exact hash, immutable reviewed bytes) was verified against the real DB. Recommend a follow-up column or approval-time record in a later pass.

Downstream invalidation beyond the intent approval is by construction only: no partition/preparation/package/evaluation artifacts exist yet (M3.2+), so only approval invalidation could be and was demonstrated.
Preview safety uses the trusted-template escaping path (React text interpolation); the opaque-origin sandbox alternative is not exercised because no code-preview content exists at the intent stage.

Ollama/live-model mode is operator-unconfigured in this runtime: only the safe needs_configuration failure is exercised end to end; live model quality, prompt robustness and live-response validation remain separate open gates.

docs/DECISIONS.md contains the M2.3 session-boundary checkpoint entry but no separate final M2.3 completion entry mirroring the provenance-line linkage design, the 403/404 read/create split and the infra allowlist widening (coordinator-owned doc; non-blocking).

Design observations accepted after challenge: provenance linkage embeds the planning request ID inside the immutable private intent bytes (scope line) with transaction-bound request/snapshot binding (no schema change); reads of a foreign intent return 403 (existence disclosed only to holders of a valid UUID) while cross-identity creates return 404 via the intake ownership check. Both are recorded here as reviewed trade-offs, not defects.
Real isolated runner (M5.2 blocked), live model, human study and delivery gates remain open; this review covers only the M2.3 scope on the synthetic runtime.
No secrets, prompts or real private fixture contents are reproduced in this report; all observations use synthetic accounts/data.
